subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a native Gateway multi-token principal model for token-mode Control UI/WebChat users, and should it be unified with the scoped-token work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367?
rationale: The request changes public auth config, credential matching, caller identity, session isolation, and authorization semantics, so code work needs maintainer security/product intent first.

options.title: Design Unified Principals
options.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model for per-user tokens, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation/revocation, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To User Labels
options.body: Implement only token-to-user labels and session identity for Control UI/WebChat now, accepting a likely later migration into broader scoped-token semantics.

options.title: Keep Front-Layer Pattern
options.body: Decline native multi-token auth for now and document trusted-proxy or Pinchy-style front layers as the supported team-deployment path.

recommendation.title: Design Unified Principals
recommendation.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model for per-user tokens, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation/revocation, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The trusted-proxy work is the existing identity-bearing Gateway auth design closest to the requested token identity boundary.
